preamble: The alveolar trill [r] loses its apical vibration and is realized as a voiced retroflex (postalveolar) fricative [ʐ]: when the tongue tip fails to make contact, the high-velocity airflow of the trill produces continuous frication. This assibilated /r/ is a hallmark of Andean Spanish, where the trill (spelled rr, or r word-initially) is commonly pronounced [ʐ], as in highland Bolivia. A similar pattern is reported for word-initial /r/ in Chicahuaxtla Triqui (Mixtecan), where the trill is less common than fricative realizations.

examples.note: Word-initial <r> was formerly described as a trill [r], but it is more commonly pronounced with frication, as voiced [ʐ] or voiceless [ʂ]; only some speakers keep the trill. Elliott et al. (2016) therefore analyse the phoneme as /ʐ/.
